title: Rabbi Natan Daroma
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin, chapter 6, end of halakhah 4, relates that Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yonatan went up to Chamat Gader and decided to wait for the elders of the South. Rabbi Natan Daroma came; they asked him and he permitted it. Resh Lakish heard and responded, etc. Hyman calls this a scribal error: the reading should follow the account in Babylonian Eruvin 65b about Resh Lakish and Rabbi Chanina’s students, who asked Rabbi Afes. As Hyman explained in his entry, although Rabbi Afes headed the academy in Tzippori after Rabbi’s death, under Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi’s patriarchate, his permanent home was in the South. Hyman finds no Rabbi Natan Daroma elsewhere.

notes.text: The Afes identification, reconstruction of the southern elders’ episode, and explanation of his residence and office are Hyman’s argument. His claim not to find another Natan Daroma is not a new exhaustive search.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:4 retains the variant (פרס) [נתן] דרומה in the southern-elders episode. Bavli Eruvin 65b separately names Resh Lakish, Rabbi Chanina’s students and Rabbi Afes. Hyman’s substitution of Afes and his southern-residence/Tzippori-office reconstruction remain his argument, not a harmonization of the two witnesses.
